llm_evaluation.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common phishing tactics such as domain spoofing, use of macro-enabled attachments, URL obfuscation via shorteners and punycode domains, and social engineering themes targeting HR, tax authorities, CEOs, and cloud storage providers. The technical details like email headers, SPF/DKIM results, SMTP logs, domain registration data, attachment analyses, and web proxy logs are plausible and consistent with real-world phishing campaigns. The inclusion of MITRE ATT&CK techniques further enhances authenticity.
llm_evaluation.consistency: The dataset maintains good consistency and schema adherence across samples. Each entry includes a scenario description, detailed technical data with relevant subfields, indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. Field naming is mostly uniform, though there is a minor inconsistency in the naming of attachment analysis fields (e.g., 'attachment_analysis' vs. 'attachment_malware_analysis'). The structure of email headers, body, and logs is consistent and well formatted. The indicators and detection methods align well with the technical data provided.
suggestions: Standardize field names for attachment analysis across all samples (e.g., always use 'attachment_analysis' or 'attachment_malware_analysis') to improve schema uniformity.
